author: Dominick Bonny
title: Fraud, Arson and Broken Dreams: Bethesda Business Manager's History Before The Church
text:
In the 1970s a popular young church with a charismatic and fashionable preacher named Larry Titus sprang up among the apple orchards of Washington State’s Wenatchee Valley. It was called Bethesda Christian Center and in addition to producing evangelical music television programming and recordings, the church started a college, owned a glossy magazine geared toward Christian women, a bookstore, a radio station and even a local gas station.
Titus and his wife Devi were known for their expensive lifestyle.
Her furs became a thing of local legend and he was always wearing expensive new suits. Then there were the Cadillacs.
Titus encouraged his followers to give everything, even their retirement savings and property. Some people did just that. Some took out second mortgages and gave the money to the church. After Larry and Devi left people lost their homes, and orchards.
Almost as well-known as Titus and his preaching was the church’s music program, specifically the “Bethesda Singers.”
The Bethesda Singers were good. They traveled all over the world to perform. They took multiple trips to “The Holy Land,” Israel and Palestine.
According to evidence presented in his trial in 1979, Bethesda’s business manager James Eyre smuggled diamonds back from one or more of those trips to Israel and used them to run a Ponzi scheme, securing “investments” from marks that included the Chelan County Sheriff at the time.
You can read my two-part series on the trial here:
The Land of Milk and Honey: Part I of the Bethesda Saga
Milk and Honey, Part 2: The Trial of Bethesda Christian Center’s Business Manager James Eyre
But this piece is about who James Eyre was as a man, and as a father, through the eyes of his son, James Eyre Jr. It’s also about his criminal history before he got to the Pacific Northwest.
What follows is a letter from the younger Eyre to Bethesda survivors. I came across it in the boxes of materials former Bethesda folks or their children have given me over the last five years. I did not edit or make any changes other than formatting and creating section headers.
Trigger warning: the subject of attempted suicide is discussed.
